subjects.name: Sachunterricht
subjects.nameEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
subjects.description: Sachunterricht is the integrated primary-school subject (Kl. 1–4; in Bayern "Heimat- und Sachunterricht") combining natural science, technology, geography, history and social studies around children's local world. There are no KMK Bildungsstandards; the GDSU Perspektivrahmen (2013) is the national reference, and from Kl. 5 the content splits into Biologie, Erdkunde, Geschichte, Politik and Naturwissenschaften.

sources.name: Perspektivrahmen Sachunterricht (Gesellschaft für Didaktik des Sachunterrichts, GDSU)
sources.version: Vollständig überarbeitete Ausgabe, Verlag Julius Klinkhardt, Bad Heilbrunn 2013 (ISBN 978-3-7815-1992-3)
sources.level: Kompetenzerwartungen bis Ende Jahrgangsstufe 4 (Beispiele für Kl. 1/2 und 3/4)
sources.notes: No KMK Bildungsstandards exist for Sachunterricht; the GDSU Perspektivrahmen is the national, non-binding reference framework that most Länder curricula follow. Code scheme: <PERSP>-DAH<n> (perspective-specific Denk-, Arbeits- und Handlungsweisen) and <PERSP>-TB<n> (Themenbereiche), PU-DAH<n> = perspektivenübergreifende DAH (ch. 3.1–3.6), VN-TB<n> = perspektivenvernetzende Themenbereiche (ch. 5.1–5.4). Verification: PU-DAH1–6 and VN-TB1–4 from the official table of contents (Klinkhardt Inhaltsverzeichnis PDF). SOWI, NAWI, GEO and TECH DAH/TB lists and numbering verified from the overview tables reproduced in the GDSU Begleitbände (Gläser/Richter 2015; Giest 2017; Adamina/Hemmer/Schubert 2016; Möller/Tenberge/Bohrmann 2021 Infodatei). HIS: three DAH (Frage-, Methoden-/Medien-, Narrationskompetenz) and four TB verified from Becher/Gläser/Pleitner 2016; TB HIS numbering inferred from that volume's explicit references (TB HIST 1 Orientierung, 2 Dauer und Wandel, 3 Alterität und Identität, 4 Fakten und Fiktion) — the volume's running text lists them in a different order, so HIS-TB2/TB3 carry some uncertainty. A revised edition ("GDSU 202x") was announced for 2024 but had not been confirmed as published in sources found; this catalogue follows the 2013 edition. Titles are short paraphrases.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Observing and Describing
topics.description: Look closely and over time at a plant, animal, object or event, notice details with several senses and describe them in words or a simple drawing, separating what was seen from what is guessed.
evidence: Describe at least four observable features of an object or living thing (colour, shape, size, texture, movement)
Produce a labelled observation drawing of something seen directly
Say what changed when observing the same thing on two occasions (e.g. a bean seedling on Monday and Friday)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a snail on a leaf for a few minutes, can they describe exactly what they saw and draw it with labels?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: describing objects orally with precise words
externalPrerequisites.reason: Observations must be put into words

osMatches.note: os includes simple equipment such as magnifiers

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Comparing and Sorting by Features
topics.description: Compare objects, materials, plants or animals and sort them into groups using a chosen feature, explaining the sorting rule — the basic Sachunterricht method of ordering the world.
evidence: Sort a collection (leaves, materials, animal pictures) into groups and name the criterion used
Re-sort the same collection by a different criterion
Explain why one item belongs to a group and another does not
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a pile of leaves from the schoolyard, can they sort them into groups and explain the rule they used?

prerequisites.reason: Sorting needs features that have first been observed

externalPrerequisites.subject: Mathematik
externalPrerequisites.concept: sorting and classifying objects by attributes
externalPrerequisites.reason: Same logical operation as in early maths

osMatches.note: os topic is limited to materials
os topic is limited to living things

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Asking Investigable Questions
topics.description: Turn curiosity about everyday phenomena into questions that can be answered by observing, trying out, asking someone or looking it up — the GDSU aim of meeting things with interest.
evidence: Formulate at least two own questions about a phenomenon shown in class
Say for a question whether it can be answered by trying it out, by asking someone or by looking it up
Pick one question and suggest a first way to find the answer
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices that puddles disappear after rain, can they ask a question about it that they could actually find out?

prerequisites.reason: Good questions arise from careful observation

osMatches.note: os topic covers historical questions only

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Making Predictions
topics.description: Before trying something out, state a prediction (Vermutung) with a reason based on prior experience, and afterwards compare the result with it.
evidence: State a prediction with a "because" reason before a test
Record the prediction (tick, drawing or sentence) before the test
Say afterwards whether the prediction was right and what was learned
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before dropping a coin, a cork and a key into water, can {{name}} say what they think will happen and why — and check afterwards?

prerequisites.reason: A prediction answers a question in advance

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Carrying Out Simple Experiments
topics.description: Carry out a simple guided experiment (Versuch) safely by following picture or step instructions, handling materials carefully and observing what happens.
evidence: Follow a 3–5 step picture instruction for an experiment without skipping steps
Follow class safety rules (goggles, no tasting, tidy workplace)
Describe what happened during the experiment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a picture card showing how to test whether salt dissolves, can they carry it out step by step and tell what happened?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Measuring in Investigations
topics.description: Use measuring instruments (ruler, measuring jug, scales, thermometer, stopwatch) in Sachunterricht investigations and read them correctly with units.
evidence: Choose a suitable instrument for a quantity (length, volume, mass, temperature, time)
Read a value correctly including the unit
Repeat a measurement and notice when results differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to find out how much a plant grew this week, can they choose the right tool, measure and write the result with its unit?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Mathematik
externalPrerequisites.concept: measuring length in cm and reading scales
externalPrerequisites.reason: Instrument reading relies on maths measurement skills

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Recording Data in Tables and Charts
topics.nameDe: Daten in Tabellen und Diagrammen festhalten
topics.description: Record observations and measurements (e.g. a weather diary or plant growth) in tables, tally charts and simple bar charts, and read off what the data show.
evidence: Fill in a prepared observation table over several days
Turn the table into a simple bar chart or pictogram
State one pattern visible in the data
topics.assessmentPrompt: After keeping a two-week weather diary, can {{name}} draw a simple chart of it and say which kind of weather was most common?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Mathematik
externalPrerequisites.concept: reading and drawing a bar chart
externalPrerequisites.reason: Chart conventions are taught in Mathematik (Daten)

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Writing an Experiment Record
topics.description: Document an experiment in the standard German school scheme Frage – Vermutung – Material – Durchführung – Beobachtung – Ergebnis, using words and sketches.
evidence: Fill in all six sections of a Versuchsprotokoll for a class experiment
Keep observation (what happened) separate from result (what it means)
Use the protocol to explain the experiment to someone who was not there
topics.assessmentPrompt: After an experiment on what dissolves in water, can {{name}} write a protocol with question, guess, materials, steps, observation and result?

prerequisites.reason: Only a performed experiment can be documented

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Protocols are a factual text type

osMatches.note: os has no fixed six-part protocol scheme
os topic is age 13-14

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Planning a Fair Test
topics.nameDe: Versuche planen: nur eine Bedingung ändern
topics.description: Plan an own experiment to answer a question, changing only one condition while keeping the others the same, and explain why this makes the comparison fair.
evidence: Name the one condition to change and the conditions to keep the same
Plan materials and steps for the test
Explain why changing two things at once would make the result unclear
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to know whether cress grows better with light, can they plan a test where only the light is different?

prerequisites.reason: A fair test checks a prediction

osMatches.note: os variable control is formalised at age 9-12

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Field Trips and Interviews
topics.description: Prepare, carry out and evaluate an exploration of a place outside school (Unterrichtsgang to a bakery, fire station, town hall) and an interview with an expert using prepared questions.
evidence: Prepare a list of questions before a visit or interview
Record answers and observations on site (notes, photos, sketches)
Report back the main findings to the class
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before a class visit to the fire station, can {{name}} prepare questions, note the answers and report what they found out?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: asking and answering questions in conversation
externalPrerequisites.reason: Interviews are oral communication

osMatches.note: os age 4-9 vs DE Kl. 2-4 (age 7-10): os earlier by ~3 yrs

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Researching Information
topics.description: Find information on a Sachunterricht question in children's non-fiction books, lexicons and child-friendly search engines (e.g. fragFINN, Blinde Kuh), and judge whether a source fits the question.
evidence: Use a table of contents, index or child search engine to find information on a topic
Note key facts in own words with the source
Say whether a found source actually answers the question
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to know what hedgehogs eat, can they find the answer in a book or a children's search engine and say where it came from?

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Sources are factual texts

osMatches.note: os focuses on reliability judgement

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Presenting Findings
topics.description: Present results of an investigation or research to the class with a poster, short talk or simple digital slide, using subject vocabulary and answering questions.
evidence: Create a poster with a heading, pictures and key facts
Give a short structured talk (2–3 minutes) using subject terms
Answer at least one question from classmates
topics.assessmentPrompt: After researching an animal, can {{name}} make a poster and give a short talk to the class about it?

prerequisites.reason: Data are often presented as charts

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Presentations are a Deutsch speaking competence

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Evaluating and Reflecting on Results
topics.description: Check whether results answer the original question, discuss possible errors, and reflect on what was learned and how the method could be improved.
evidence: Say whether the result answers the question asked
Name one possible source of error or uncertainty
Suggest one improvement for a repeat investigation
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a class experiment gives mixed results, can {{name}} say what might have gone wrong and how to do it better next time?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Living and Non-Living Things
topics.description: Tell living things from non-living things using signs of life: they feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, move or react, and they die.
evidence: Sort pictures into living and non-living
Name at least three signs of life
Explain why a plant counts as living even though it does not walk
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a tree is alive but a stone is not?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Parts of a Plant
topics.description: Name the parts of a flowering plant — Wurzel, Sprossachse/Stängel, Blatt, Blüte — and state the main job of each.
evidence: Label root, stem, leaf and flower on a real plant or drawing
State one job of each part (e.g. roots take up water)
Find the same parts on a different plant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} pulls up a dandelion, can they name its parts and say what the roots do?

prerequisites.reason: Plants are first recognised as living things

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Germination and Plant Growth
topics.description: Grow beans or cress and find out that seeds need water and warmth to germinate, while the growing plant also needs light — observed in a classroom growth experiment.
evidence: Describe the stages from seed to seedling (swelling, root, shoot, first leaves)
Name the conditions needed for germination and for further growth
Predict what happens to a seedling kept in the dark
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plants cress on wet cotton wool, can they say what it needs to sprout and why it turns yellow in a dark cupboard?

prerequisites.reason: Growth is described via plant parts

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Early Spring Flowers
topics.description: Recognise common early-spring flowers (Schneeglöckchen, Krokus, Tulpe, Narzisse) and explain that they bloom early because they store food in bulbs or tubers.
evidence: Name and recognise at least three Frühblüher
Point out the bulb (Zwiebel) and explain it stores food
Explain why Frühblüher can bloom before the trees have leaves
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees crocuses in March, can they name them and explain how they can flower so early?

prerequisites.reason: Bulbs are a modified plant part
Linked to the course of the year

osMatches.note: os has no storage-organ / early bloomer topic

topics.laenderNotes: Classic Kl. 1/2 spring unit in almost all Länder.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Meadow and Hedge Habitats
topics.description: Explore a local meadow or hedge, name typical plants and animals living there and explain that they depend on this habitat for food and shelter.
evidence: Name at least three plants and three animals found in a meadow or hedge
Say what one animal finds there (food, shelter, nesting place)
Explain what would happen to the animals if the meadow were mown or the hedge removed
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a walk to a meadow, can {{name}} name animals living there and explain why they need the meadow?

prerequisites.reason: Plants are identified by their parts

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Keeping Pets Responsibly
topics.description: Describe the needs of a common pet (guinea pig, rabbit, cat, dog, budgie) and what species-appropriate keeping (artgerechte Haltung) means for feeding, space, company and care.
evidence: List the needs of one pet (food, water, space, company, exercise)
Explain why rabbits or guinea pigs should not be kept alone
Name daily and weekly care tasks and who is responsible
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants a guinea pig, can they explain what it needs to be kept well and why one alone is not enough?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Farm Animals and Their Products
topics.description: Name farm animals (cow, pig, hen, sheep), the products we get from them (milk, eggs, meat, wool) and basic conditions of keeping, e.g. free-range vs. barn hens.
evidence: Match farm animals to their products
Describe the path of milk from cow to supermarket in 3–4 steps
Compare two ways of keeping hens (Freiland, Bodenhaltung) using the egg code
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which animal gives us wool, milk and eggs, and what the number on an egg tells you?
topics.laenderNotes: EU egg code (0–3) is taught widely in German Grundschule.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: The Hedgehog
topics.description: Describe the hedgehog's body, food (insects, snails, worms) and nocturnal life, and its hibernation in a leaf pile — the classic autumn animal of German primary school.
evidence: Describe hedgehog features (spines, snout, rolling up for protection)

topics.description: Complete the school cycling training (Radfahrausbildung) with the police, often at a Jugendverkehrsschule, and pass the theory and practical test in real traffic to receive the cycling licence (Fahrradpass/Fahrradführerschein).
evidence: Pass a theory test on traffic rules and signs
Ride a set route in real or simulated traffic applying all rules

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Environment-Friendly Mobility

Suggest a realistic change in the family's mobility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why walking or cycling to school is better than being driven, and when the car makes sense?

topics.name: Time Words and Daily Routine

evidence: Order pictures of a daily routine and narrate it
Use gestern/heute/morgen correctly in sentences
Answer "what happens before / after ..." questions about the school day
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what they did yesterday, what they do today and what will happen tomorrow, using the right words?

evidence: Name the days of the week and the months in order
Find a date and the day of the week on a calendar
Place birthdays, holidays and seasons on a Jahreskreis
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find their birthday on the calendar and say which day of the week and season it falls in?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht

Arrange events of the own life in order on a timeline
Explain what the source tells about the past
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} make a timeline of their life with photos from baby to now and explain each step?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht

Imagine and describe how one thing might look in the future

topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Schule früher" for Kl. 1/2; many schools visit a Schulmuseum.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: History or Story?

Point out a feature that shows a story is invented
Explain that stories can still contain true details about the past

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Family Tree and Generations

evidence: Draw a family tree with three generations
Use kinship terms correctly
Retell one thing a grandparent experienced as a child
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw their family tree and tell you one thing about their grandparents' childhood?
topics.laenderNotes: Should be handled sensitively for children in diverse family situations.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Festivals and Days of Remembrance
topics.description: Explain the origin and meaning of festivals and commemorative days celebrated in Germany — e.g. Sankt Martin, Erntedank, Karneval, Tag der Deutschen Einheit (3 October) — and how traditions change.
evidence: Place festivals and commemoration days on the calendar
Explain the historical or religious origin of at least two of them
Explain what is commemorated on 3 October

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Historical Sources

Ask at least three questions of a source (who, when, why made?)
Explain the difference between a source and a schoolbook account

topics.subject: Sachunterricht

Record and summarise the main answers
Compare two eyewitness accounts and explain why they may differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} interview their grandmother about her school days and report what they found out?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Historical Timeline
topics.description: Place historical periods and events on a timeline using years, decades, centuries and millennia, and understand counting years before and after the birth of Christ (v. Chr. / n. Chr.).
evidence: Place given events correctly on a timeline with a scale
Use Jahrzehnt, Jahrhundert and Jahrtausend correctly
Explain v. Chr. and n. Chr. and order dates across year 0
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} place the Stone Age, the Romans, the knights and their own birth year on a class timeline in the right order?

externalPrerequisites.reason: Years and scales require larger numbers

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Life in the Stone Age

Explain the change to farming and settled life (Sesshaftigkeit) as a slow process
Name a find that tells us about Stone Age life and what it reveals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a Stone Age family lived and how life changed when people started farming?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Romans in Germania and the Limes
topics.nameDe: Die Römer in Germanien und der Limes
topics.description: Describe Roman presence in what is now Germany — the Limes frontier, forts and towns such as Köln, Trier or Augsburg, trade with Germanic tribes — and traces still visible today (roads, words, ruins).

Compare everyday life of Romans and Germanic peoples
Name Roman traces in today's language, towns or landscape
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Limes was and name something the Romans left behind in Germany?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Knights, Castles and the Middle Ages

Compare the life of a knight, a peasant and a craftsman
Name a medieval trace in the home region (castle, town wall, church)

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: History of Our Town
topics.description: Investigate the history of the home town using local sources — old photos and maps, street names, the town chronicle, the Heimatmuseum, monuments — and describe how the place has changed.
evidence: Compare an old and a current photo or map of the same place
Explain the origin of a street or place name
Present one stage of the town's history after a museum or archive visit
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find out from old photos how their town centre has changed and explain where a street name comes from?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Die Geschichte unseres Schulortes" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: History in Media
topics.description: Examine how films, computer games, comics and toys show the past, and distinguish realistic from invented or exaggerated elements by comparing them with sources.
evidence: Identify invented elements in a film or game scene set in the past
Check a media depiction against a source or factual text
Explain why media may change history (entertainment, simplification)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a cartoon about knights, can {{name}} point out what is probably made up and how they could check it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Telling History

evidence: Write or present a short historical account based on sources
Mark which statements are certain and which are assumptions
Name the sources the account is based on
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a project on the town's history, can {{name}} tell the story in their own words and say how they know?

topics.name: Me and My Identity

Name at least two own strengths
Name something that makes a classmate special
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you three things they are good at and one thing they are still learning?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Different Kinds of Families

evidence: Describe at least four different family forms without judgement
Name tasks family members do for each other
Explain that what makes a family is caring for each other
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that families can look very different and still be families?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Friendship
topics.description: Describe what makes a good friendship (trust, helping, sharing, forgiving), how friendships can change, and how to include others.
evidence: Name qualities of a good friend
Describe how to make up after an argument with a friend
Suggest how to include a child who is left out
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what makes someone a good friend and what to do if a friendship goes wrong?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Agreeing Class Rules

Explain what would happen without rules
Help decide on a fair consequence for breaking a rule
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the class has a rule about listening and how the class agreed on it?

topics.name: Resolving Conflicts Peacefully

Find a solution to a role-play conflict that both sides accept

Explain what a majority is

topics.name: Needs and Wants

Distinguish goods from services with examples
Explain why not all wishes can be fulfilled
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between needing a warm coat and wanting new trainers?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Understanding Advertising

Explain at least three tricks used in adverts for children
Compare an advertised product with its reality
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} spot the tricks in a toy advert and explain why it makes them want the toy?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht

Justify a buying decision with reasons

Follow up whether a decision was implemented
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the class council works and lead a short discussion as chair?

Explain why individual and common interests can conflict
topics.assessmentPrompt: If there are fewer footballs than children, can {{name}} suggest a fair rule and explain why it is fair?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Electing a Class Representative

evidence: List the tasks of a class representative
Conduct a secret election and count the results
Explain why the vote is secret
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the class representative was elected and what they are supposed to do?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: Children's Rights

Explain the right to participation with a school example
Describe a situation where a child's right is violated and who can help

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.name: The Municipality

topics.name: Elections in a Democracy

Explain who is elected at municipal and federal level
Compare a class election with a real election

Suggest how to respond to a prejudiced remark

Explain why avoiding waste is better than recycling it

Name where batteries and old devices must be returned

clusters.summary: Your child is learning what makes something alive.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, was Lebewesen von Nicht-Lebendigem unterscheidet.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about plants and animals nearby — early spring flowers, the hedgehog, birds in winter, pets and farm animals — and how seeds grow.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Pflanzen und Tiere der Umgebung kennen – Frühblüher, Igel, Vögel im Winter, Haus- und Nutztiere – und wie aus Samen Pflanzen wachsen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to identify trees and insects, understand food chains, the forest and pond as habitats, and how animals are adapted.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Bäume und Insekten zu bestimmen, Nahrungsketten, den Lebensraum Wald und Gewässer sowie die Angepasstheit von Tieren zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the four seasons and how nature changes through the year.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die vier Jahreszeiten und die Veränderungen in der Natur kennen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring materials, floating and sinking, air, magnets and the weather, and learning how to behave in case of fire.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erforscht Stoffe, Schwimmen und Sinken, Luft, Magnete und das Wetter und lernt das richtige Verhalten im Brandfall.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is investigating water (states, cycle, dissolving, filtering), fire, simple electric circuits and magnetic poles through experiments.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind untersucht in Versuchen Wasser (Aggregatzustände, Kreislauf, Lösen, Filtern), Feuer, einfache Stromkreise und Magnetpole.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to name body parts and feelings.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Körperteile und Gefühle zu benennen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about the senses, teeth and tooth brushing, healthy food, hygiene, setting body boundaries and how to make an emergency call.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Sinne, Zähne und Zahnpflege, gesunde Ernährung, Hygiene, das Setzen von Grenzen und wie man einen Notruf absetzt.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the skeleton, heart, lungs and digestion work, about puberty and where babies come from, first aid and addiction prevention.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Skelett, Herz, Lunge und Verdauung funktionieren, erfährt etwas über Pubertät und die Entstehung des Lebens, Erste Hilfe und Suchtvorbeugung.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to use tools safely, build from instructions, make towers stable and vehicles roll, and finds out about different jobs.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Werkzeuge sicher zu nutzen, nach Anleitung zu bauen, standfeste Türme und rollende Fahrzeuge zu konstruieren, und erkundet Berufe.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is building stable bridges, exploring levers and gears, taking devices apart and learning how inventions and machines changed work.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind baut stabile Brücken, erforscht Hebel und Zahnräder, untersucht Geräte und lernt, wie Erfindungen und Maschinen die Arbeit verändert haben.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring school and home town, drawing maps of familiar places and comparing town and countryside.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erkundet Schule und Wohnort, zeichnet Pläne vertrauter Räume und vergleicht Stadt und Land.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read maps with key, scale and grid, use a compass, and get to know the own Bundesland, Germany, Europe and the globe.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Karten mit Legende, Maßstab und Planquadraten zu lesen, den Kompass zu nutzen und das eigene Bundesland, Deutschland, Europa und den Globus kennen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to cross the road safely.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, sicher über die Straße zu gehen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the safe way to school, to be seen in the dark, the most important traffic signs and first cycling skills.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt den sicheren Schulweg, wie man im Dunkeln gesehen wird, wichtige Verkehrszeichen und erste Fahrradfertigkeiten.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is doing the cycling training with the police: roadworthy bike, right-of-way rules, turning left and the cycling test.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind absolviert die Radfahrausbildung mit der Polizei: verkehrssicheres Fahrrad, Vorfahrtsregeln, Linksabbiegen und die Fahrradprüfung.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning words for time and the order of the day.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Zeitbegriffe und den Ablauf des Tages.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the calendar, their own life story on a timeline and how life used to be compared with today.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt den Kalender, stellt die eigene Lebensgeschichte auf einer Zeitleiste dar und vergleicht früher und heute.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is working with historical sources and eyewitnesses, placing the Stone Age, Romans and Middle Ages on a timeline, and exploring local history.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit Quellen und Zeitzeugen, ordnet Steinzeit, Römer und Mittelalter auf der Zeitleiste ein und erforscht die Geschichte des Wohnortes.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to describe themselves and their strengths.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, sich selbst und seine Stärken zu beschreiben.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about families and friendship, agreeing class rules, solving conflicts, voting and the difference between needs and wants.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Familien und Freundschaft, Klassenregeln, Konfliktlösung, Abstimmungen und den Unterschied zwischen Bedürfnissen und Wünschen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about the class council and elections, children's rights, how the municipality works, advertising, and respect for diversity.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Klassenrat und Wahlen, Kinderrechte, die Aufgaben der Gemeinde, Werbung und den respektvollen Umgang mit Vielfalt kennen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to avoid and sort waste and to save energy in everyday life.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Müll zu vermeiden und zu trennen und im Alltag Energie zu sparen.

clusters.subject: Sachunterricht
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about recycling and Pfand, renewable energy, climate protection, nature protection, regional food and fair trade.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Recycling und Pfand, erneuerbare Energien, Klima- und Naturschutz, regionale Lebensmittel und fairen Handel.
